name: reconya
description: Network reconnaissance and asset discovery tool
readme_summary: ReconYa is a Go-based network reconnaissance and asset discovery tool designed for network administrators and security professionals. It provides real-time monitoring of local network devices, including IPv4 scanning and IPv6 passive monitoring, with features like device identification, port scanning, and alerting.
key_features: IPv4 network scanning (ICMP sweeps, TCP probes, ARP)
IPv6 passive monitoring (neighbor discovery, interface monitoring)
Device identification (MAC, vendor, hostname, OS fingerprinting)
Port scanning with service detection and banner grabbing
Alerting for network events (new devices, risky ports, unreachable hosts)
Web console with topology map and live event log
Multi-network support
Zero outbound calls by default
primary_use_case: Real-time network device discovery, monitoring, and asset management for network administrators and security professionals.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant digital cartographer meticulously mapping a bustling, interconnected cityscape at night. The cartographer uses a glowing, magnifying glass to reveal hidden details on each building (representing network devices), such as glowing windows (open ports) and subtle labels indicating their function (hostnames/OS). Data streams flow from the city towards the cartographer's console, which displays a dynamic network topology map. Small, subtle UI elements with the 'reconYa' logo are visible on the console. The scene is rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style with a dark, tech-noir color palette, emphasizing discovery and security.

name: agent-orchestrator
description: Run and supervise teams of coding agents from planning to merge. Any harness (Claude code, codex, +25 more). Desktop, web, mobile, and cloud agents.
readme_summary: Agent Orchestrator (AO) is a local desktop application designed to manage and supervise teams of coding agents. It provides a unified workspace for planning, running, and monitoring agent-driven development tasks, from initial planning to code merging.
key_features: Run and supervise teams of coding agents
Supports various coding agents (Claude code, Codex, etc.)
Handles desktop, web, mobile, and cloud agents
Provides a project-aware orchestrator for planning and delegation
Assigns each agent its own branch and worktree for Git-backed work
Tracks task, conversation, terminal, files, preview, PR, CI, and review status
Offers a live Kanban view of agent activity and project status
Local daemon monitors agent activity and source-control state
primary_use_case: To provide a unified, local desktop workspace for managing and orchestrating multiple coding agents to collaboratively develop software projects, streamlining the entire development lifecycle from planning to merge.
cover_image_prompt: A conductor leading a symphony orchestra, where each musician is a distinct coding agent (represented by stylized robots or drones). The conductor, holding a tablet displaying the 'Agent Orchestrator' logo, directs the agents who are collaboratively building a complex, glowing structure representing software code. Musical notes transform into lines of code and data streams flowing between agents. In the background, a large, dynamic Kanban board visually tracks the progress of different coding tasks. The scene is a modern, well-lit studio with subtle UI elements and digital particles indicating active processes. Style: 3D isometric illustration with vibrant colors and clear, distinct elements.

name: pixel2motion
description: AI logo animation skill: turn raster logos into smooth SVG animation, animated HTML demos, GIF/video previews, and motion QA evidence.
readme_summary: Pixel2Motion is an AI-powered tool that transforms raster logos into smooth, animated SVG logos. It generates interactive HTML demos, GIF/video previews, and motion QA evidence, streamlining the process of creating brand motion graphics and SVG animations.
key_features: Raster logo to SVG conversion
SVG logo animation generation
Interactive HTML motion demos
GIF/video preview exports
Motion QA evidence
AI-assisted brand motion
primary_use_case: Automating the creation of animated logos and brand motion graphics from static raster images, with outputs suitable for web and development use.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled artisan, depicted as a digital sculptor, meticulously chiseling a rough, pixelated block of stone (representing a raster logo) into a smooth, flowing SVG form. As the SVG form emerges, it begins to glow and animate, transforming into a dynamic logo with subtle light trails and particles. In the background, a clean, modern interface displays code snippets and a preview of the animated logo. The scene is set in a bright, airy studio with a focus on the transformation process. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, vibrant color palette, emphasizing the transition from static to dynamic.

name: demo-ghostprovider
description: TUI for automation of deploying and self-hosting
readme_summary: GhostProvider is a Rust-based TUI application that automates the deployment and self-hosting of services. It simplifies the process by allowing users to deploy supported applications from GitHub URLs as systemd user services, ensuring local data storage and no root privileges are required.
key_features: One-Click Deploy from GitHub URL
Systemd User Service Management (no root required)
Local data storage and compile-time host allowlist for security
Automated build tool provisioning
System scan for prerequisites and port conflicts
Full control panel for deployed services (start, stop, restart, remove)
Supports VERT, SearXNG, and Memos
primary_use_case: Simplifying the self-hosting of specific applications by automating their deployment as systemd user services.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, stylized robot arm gently placing a neatly organized set of building blocks (labeled VERT, SearXNG, Memos) onto a clean, minimalist desk. Beside the blocks, a single GitHub URL card is being fed into a small, glowing slot on the robot's base, which then emits clean, organized systemd unit files. The background is a soft, abstract representation of a local network, emphasizing privacy and control. The overall mood is one of effortless automation and secure, local operation. 3D isometric illustration style with a bright, clean color palette.

name: beautiful-mermaid
readme_summary: Beautiful-mermaid is a TypeScript library that renders Mermaid diagrams into visually appealing SVGs or ASCII art. It offers ultra-fast, themeable diagram generation with zero DOM dependencies, making it suitable for both rich UIs and terminal environments.
key_features: Supports 6 diagram types (Flowcharts, State, Sequence, Class, ER, XY Charts)
Dual output: SVG for UIs, ASCII/Unicode for terminals
Synchronous rendering for immediate output
15 built-in themes and easy custom theme creation
Full Shiki compatibility for VS Code theme integration
Live theme switching via CSS custom properties
Mono mode for minimal color diagrams
Zero DOM dependencies, pure TypeScript
Ultra-fast rendering performance
primary_use_case: To provide developers with a fast, customizable, and versatile library for rendering text-based diagrams (Mermaid) into both graphical (SVG) and terminal-friendly (ASCII) formats, enhancing visualization in various environments.
cover_image_prompt: A master artisan, holding a glowing chisel, meticulously carving intricate, colorful SVG blueprints from rough, unformed blocks of text. Beside the artisan, a separate, smaller section shows the same text being transformed into a clean, minimalist ASCII art sculpture, perfectly suited for a dark, futuristic terminal screen. Subtle digital particles and faint code snippets float around the scene, hinting at the underlying technology. The overall mood is one of precision and creative transformation. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a vibrant yet focused color palette, emphasizing the dual output capability of 'beautiful-mermaid'.
